result.summary: Introduces a reachability-tracking framework for fuzz targets to record whether specific execution goals are satisfied across a corpus run. Targets declare `ReachabilityGoal` instances and report whether conditions were hit using `ObserveReachabilityGoal()`. An environment variable, `FUZZ_ENFORCE_REACHABILITY=1`, causes the fuzz binary to fail on process exit if any registered goal was not reached.
result.problem: Corpus replay CI verifies that test inputs do not crash or trigger sanitizers, but it cannot detect if corpus or code changes silently cause high-value internal execution paths (such as successful handshakes, valid transaction packages, or block index mutations) to stop being reached.
evidence: Commit bcf97a3cc4: "This allows corpus CI to detect lost path coverage without a separate build configuration."
Follow-up to merged PR #35482 ('fuzz: exercise the transaction-handling path in process_message(s)').
result.scope_notes: Adds helper utilities in `src/test/fuzz/util/reachability.{h,cpp}` and instruments 11 fuzz targets with reachability assertions.
result.card: Adds reachability goal tracking across fuzz target runs, letting fuzz test harnesses verify that critical execution paths are actually exercised by a corpus. Setting FUZZ_ENFORCE_REACHABILITY=1 forces the process to exit with an error on shutdown if any registered goal was never reached. This allows corpus regression testing in CI to catch lost path coverage without needing custom instrumentation or separate coverage-build runs. Eleven fuzz targets are instrumented with goals covering transaction validation, P2P handshakes, compact block reconstruction, and mempool loading.
